messages.text: We already get food stamps. Can my 3 year old also get WIC?

Yes, a 3-year-old can often get WIC. Children can get it until they turn 5. Getting food stamps (SNAP) can also help, because it often counts toward WIC's income rules.

I need a few details to check your household:

1. Who lives with you and shares food? Please give their ages. Is anyone pregnant, breastfeeding, or had a baby in the last year?
2. About how much income does the household get each month before taxes, and how often is it paid?

Me, my husband, and our son. I'm 28, he's 30, and our son is 3. Nobody's pregnant and I haven't had a baby in the last year.

My husband makes $2,500 a month before taxes. I'm not sure how often he gets paid, I think it's monthly? I don't have any other income.

**Yes, your son will likely qualify for WIC.**

**Why:**
- WIC serves children from age 1 until their 5th birthday, so a 3-year-old fits. ([7 CFR 246.2, WIC definitions](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2))
- Your family already gets food stamps (SNAP). That automatically meets WIC's income test. ([7 CFR 246.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.7))
- WIC also does a short health and nutrition check at the clinic. ([7 CFR 246.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.7))

**How to apply:**
- Go to a local health department clinic, or call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942).
- Website: [Tennessee Department of Health WIC](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html)
- Bring proof that you get SNAP if you have it. The clinic will tell you what else to bring.

**Health coverage for your son:** The screening also shows he is likely eligible for TennCare/CoverKids. Your household income of $2,500 a month is under the $3,233 limit for a child aged 1 to 5 in a family of 3. ([TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))
- It looks unlikely for you and your husband. The limit for parents is $2,277 a month, and your income is over it. You can still apply.
- To apply, go to [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701.

For free local help, you can dial 211.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and anyone can apply.
